Rule to remember: a host that has link but cannot reach its own gateway - check the access VLAN of its port before anything else.

Correct. R1's P column is blank, show standby says 'Preemption disabled' and the interface configuration has no standby 10 preempt line. A router that comes up while another is already Active stays Standby unless it is allowed to preempt, whatever its priority.
Preempt on R2 only allows R2 to take over from an Active router with a lower priority than its own. It does not stop a higher-priority router that is configured to preempt from taking over.

explanation: Nothing is broken between the routers: each sees the other, and the group, virtual IP and priorities are as designed. While R1 was reloading, R2 correctly took over as Active. When R1 came back it had the higher priority (110 against 100), but HSRP does not hand the Active role back automatically. Preemption is off by default, and R1 shows a blank P column, 'Preemption disabled' and no standby 10 preempt line in its configuration, so it waits as Standby until R2 fails. R2's own preempt setting is irrelevant because its priority is lower. Adding standby 10 preempt on R1 makes it take over immediately. Rule to remember: priority chooses the winner of an election, preempt allows a new election to be forced.
